subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance permanently use this new opt-in configuration plus the command queue's synchronous onTaskTimeout fence, or should it be folded into an existing host timeout/cancellation contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but repository policy sets a high bar for new configuration and shared lifecycle APIs; source review cannot decide the permanent product and ownership contract.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Accept the disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue callback, and host-owned fence as the canonical maintenance timeout design, then refresh the branch against current main and merge after owner sign-off.

options.title: Reuse an existing timeout contract
options.body: Rework maintenance around the existing compaction safety budget or another established abort contract, with explicit fresh-install and upgrade behavior and without a parallel configuration surface.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the linked issue open while maintainers define a cooperative context-engine cancellation API and the permitted behavior of non-cooperative plugins.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Accept the disabled-by-default setting, synchronous queue callback, and host-owned fence as the canonical maintenance timeout design, then refresh the branch against current main and merge after owner sign-off.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history and discussion connect this person most directly to the deferred-maintenance lifecycle and its owner boundary.
